stem: A platform team is writing the standard for how new tables should be declared, and has to justify a default rather than leave each squad to choose. They care about running cost and about not hand-scheduling upkeep.

option_texts.A: Prefer managed tables, which cost less and maintain and optimize themselves automatically
option_texts.B: Prefer external tables, since keeping the files outside is what lowers the running cost
option_texts.C: Prefer external tables, because only they stay reachable from clients outside the platform
option_texts.D: Leave it open, because the two types differ only in who holds the storage path

drill_answer_short: Managed tables are the default and recommended type: cheaper to store and query, and self-maintaining
decision_hinge: Managed tables are the default and recommended table type, and compared with external tables managed tables cost less to store and query, maintain and optimize themselves automatically, and stay accessible to external clients through open APIs.

plausible_options.B: They care about running cost and about not hand-scheduling upkeep

eliminated_by.C: has to justify a default rather than leave each squad to choose
eliminated_by.D: writing the standard for how new tables should be declared

distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling - external tables are a real choice, but they are the dearer one to store and query
distractor_traps.C: T1: fabricated - managed tables stay reachable to external clients through open APIs
distractor_traps.D: T5: common misconception - the types also differ in cost, upkeep and lifecycle

stem: Reporting habits on a large table shift every few months as new dashboards land, and the team is tired of revisiting its layout choice by hand each time. They want the layout to follow however the table is actually being read.

option_texts.A: Pick the columns once from today's dashboards, since read patterns settle quickly
option_texts.B: Let the platform select and update the clustering keys as query patterns change
option_texts.C: Re-run a layout command weekly, because only a schedule can track changing reads
option_texts.D: Partition on the busiest column, because partitions adapt as the reads move around

drill_answer_short: Automatic liquid clustering selects and updates clustering keys as query patterns change
decision_hinge: Predictive optimization automatically selects and updates clustering keys as query patterns change to improve performance and lower costs.

plausible_options.C: tired of revisiting its layout choice by hand each time

eliminated_by.A: Reporting habits on a large table shift every few months as new dashboards land
eliminated_by.D: They want the layout to follow however the table is actually being read

distractor_traps.A: T4: breaks a stated requirement - a one-off choice is exactly the hand revisiting being avoided
distractor_traps.C: T3: confusable sibling - a schedule re-runs the work but still uses whichever keys were chosen by hand
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated - partitions are fixed at definition and do not adapt to reads

stem: A department has ten employees recorded, but two of them have no salary captured yet. A report computes the mean salary per department and the team must say what the figure is divided by.

option_texts.A: Ten, with the two blanks read as zero before the mean is computed
option_texts.B: Ten, because every recorded employee counts toward the mean of the group
option_texts.C: Eight, because the aggregate is computed over the non-null values in the group
option_texts.D: Nothing, because a group holding a blank yields a null figure overall

drill_answer_short: avg returns the mean calculated from the values of the group, ignoring null values
decision_hinge: The avg aggregate function returns the mean calculated from values of a group, and null values within the group are ignored.

plausible_options.A: two of them have no salary captured yet

eliminated_by.B: the team must say what the figure is divided by
eliminated_by.D: A report computes the mean salary per department

distractor_traps.A: T3: confusable sibling - treating a blank as zero is what a fillna would do first
distractor_traps.B: T5: common misconception - the divisor counts the values present, not the rows
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated - a single null does not poison the whole aggregate

stem: Booking events arrive stamped in UTC, and a regional report has to show each one in the local wall-clock time of its airport. The team is choosing the function that performs that shift.

option_texts.A: cast to timestamp, which resolves the zone from the session that reads it
option_texts.B: to_utc_timestamp, which moves the stamp into the zone the report needs
option_texts.C: date_format, which prints the stamp using a pattern that names the zone
option_texts.D: from_utc_timestamp, which renders the stamp in the named time zone

drill_answer_short: from_utc_timestamp renders a UTC timestamp in the supplied time zone
decision_hinge: The from_utc_timestamp function returns the timestamp expr rendered in the time zone given by the timezone argument.

plausible_options.B: has to show each one in the local wall-clock time of its airport

eliminated_by.A: The team is choosing the function that performs that shift
eliminated_by.C: Booking events arrive stamped in UTC

distractor_traps.A: T5: common misconception - a cast does not apply a named zone conversion
distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling - that function converts the other way, into UTC
distractor_traps.C: T2: scope error - formatting changes how a value prints without shifting the instant
